title: Odría Consolidates Military Rule
note: National Security Law, banning of APRA and Communists, and export-led growth under Odría well documented.

title: Peru Anchovy Fisheries Boom Begins
note: Peru's anchovy/fishmeal boom and rise to world's largest fishmeal producer in this period is well established.

title: Women Gain Voting Rights in Peru
note: Law N° 12391 passed 7 September 1955; limited to literate women of legal age. First exercise of the vote was 17 June 1956. All facts correct.

title: Nixon Visit Sparks Anti-U.S. Protests in Lima
note: Nixon's May 1958 Latin America tour included Lima; protests and stone-throwing at his motorcade are historically documented.

title: La Convención Valley Peasant Mobilizations
note: Hugo Blanco's Trotskyist-led land occupations in Cusco's La Convención valley circa 1960-1963 are well documented.

title: Military Coup Prevents APRA Electoral Victory
note: Coup on July 18, 1962 by General Ricardo Pérez Godoy confirmed. Minor nuance: no candidate reached the required one-third threshold; APRA (Haya) led but needed congressional resolution — not simply 'poised to form a government'.

title: Fernando Belaúnde Terry Elected President
note: 1963 election result and platform accurately described.

title: MIR and ELN Guerrilla Insurgencies Suppressed
note: MIR and ELN insurgencies launched and crushed in 1965 is documented.

title: Velasco Alvarado Military Coup and Revolution
note: Coup confirmed October 3, 1968. Nationalist-reformist motivation and sweeping reforms accurately described.

title: IPC Expropriation: Talara Act Asserts Oil Sovereignty
note: Act of Talara expropriation of IPC refinery days after the coup is confirmed. Hickenlooper Amendment threat documented.

title: Sweeping Agrarian Reform Dismantles Hacienda System
note: Decree Law 17716 issued June 24, 1969. Total expropriated land was ~9 million hectares (not 8.6M), but this is a minor discrepancy within rounding range of various sources. Cooperative structure and disappointing productivity outcomes confirmed.

title: Ancash Earthquake Kills 70,000 People
note: May 31, 1970; Mw 7.9; 66,000–70,000 deaths; buried Yungay. All key facts confirmed.

title: Fisheries Nationalization Coincides with Anchoveta Collapse
note: Pesca Perú nationalization and simultaneous El Niño-driven anchovy collapse in 1972 are well documented.

title: Sendero Luminoso Consolidates in Ayacucho
note: Guzmán's clandestine Maoist organization-building at University of Huamanga through the early 1970s is documented. 'Fourth sword of Marxism' characterization confirmed.

title: Morales Bermúdez Coup Ends Radical Military Revolution
note: Coup (Tacnazo) on August 29, 1975 confirmed. Reversal of Velasco-era reforms and IMF engagement confirmed.

title: IMF Stabilization Program Imposes Austerity
note: IMF stabilization agreement, austerity measures, recession and wage falls under Morales Bermúdez confirmed.

title: General Strike Forces Democratic Transition Announcement
note: July 1977 general strike and subsequent announcement of constituent assembly elections confirmed.

title: Constituent Assembly Grants Universal Suffrage
note: Constituent assembly elected June 18, 1978; APRA plurality; Haya de la Torre elected president of assembly; new 1979 constitution extended voting rights to illiterates. All confirmed.

title: Sendero Luminoso Launches Armed Campaign
note: Ballot box burning in Chuschi on May 17, 1980, the eve of elections, confirmed. Death toll of ~69,000 from TRC confirmed.

title: Belaúnde Returns in Democratic Elections
note: Belaúnde wins 1980 election and succeeds military government as described. Confirmed.

title: Military Enters Counterinsurgency Against Sendero
note: State of emergency in Ayacucho and military deployment with broad powers in late 1982 confirmed by TRC.

title: MRTA Founded as Second Guerrilla Organization
note: MRTA founded 1983 from remnants of MIR. Named after Túpac Amaru II. Nationalist-Marxist orientation and distinction from Sendero confirmed.

title: Ayacucho Massacres Document Systematic Atrocities
note: Socos and Pucayacu massacres in 1984 documented by TRC as crimes against humanity. Confirmed.

title: Alan García Elected: APRA's First Presidency
note: García won with 45% in first round; opponent Barrantes withdrew so no second round was held. The event claims '53 percent of the first-round vote' — this is incorrect; he received ~45% in round 1. However, he was declared winner by default when Barrantes withdrew. Minor factual error on percentage but overall narrative correct.

title: García Limits Debt Service to 10% of Export Revenue
note: 10% of export revenues debt cap, IMF ineligibility, and subsequent capital flight confirmed.

title: El Frontón Prison Massacre
note: June 18-19, 1986 confirmed. Death toll across three prisons (Lurigancho, El Frontón, Santa Bárbara) was 224-300; Sendero prisoners involved. APRA Socialist International congress timing confirmed. Note: it was a Socialist International congress (APRA was SI member), not exclusively the 'APRA International Socialist meeting'.

title: Hyperinflation Reaches Crisis Levels Under García
note: 1988 annual inflation ~1,722%, 1989 ~2,775% (event says 'nearly 3,000%' — close enough). Real wage collapse confirmed.

title: Fujimori Defeats Vargas Llosa in Presidential Runoff
note: Fujimori won runoff with ~62% vs Vargas Llosa ~38%. APRA tactical support and outsider voter coalition confirmed.

title: Fujishock: Economic Shock Therapy Ends Hyperinflation
note: Shock program launched after July 28, 1990 inauguration, contradicting campaign pledge, confirmed.

title: Cholera Epidemic Exposes Public Health Collapse
note: Cholera first appeared in late January 1991 from coastal fishing communities; first in Western Hemisphere in ~100 years. Spread pattern confirmed.

title: Autogolpe: Fujimori Dissolves Congress and Courts
note: April 5, 1992 confirmed. Military backing, OAS condemnation, ~73% domestic approval confirmed.

title: Capture of Abimael Guzmán Breaks Sendero Luminoso
note: September 12, 1992; GEIN operation in Surquillo, Lima confirmed.

title: Fujimori's New Constitution Entrenches Presidential Power
note: Referendum October 31, 1993; passed 52.3% vs 47.7%. Unicameral congress, reelection provision confirmed.

title: Economic Boom Driven by Mining Privatization
note: Peru's GDP growth exceeding 12% in 1994-1995 and mining/privatization investment boom confirmed.

title: Cenepa War with Ecuador Over Border Dispute
note: January 26 – February 28, 1995. Peru military advantage confirmed. 1998 Brasília Presidential Act peace agreement confirmed. Minor note: cease-fire was February 17, 1995, not end of February.

title: Amnesty Law Shields Military from Human Rights Prosecution
note: June 1995 amnesty law, Barrios Altos/La Cantuta coverage, Inter-American Court ruling confirmed.

title: MRTA Seizes Japanese Embassy Hostages
note: December 17, 1996 confirmed. Initially 600+ hostages; reduced to 72 who were held 126 days. Event says '72 hostages' which is accurate for those held long-term.

title: Japanese Embassy Rescue Operation Ends Hostage Crisis
note: April 22, 1997 confirmed. However the event states 'killing all 14 MRTA members and rescuing all but one of the 72 hostages.' Actual casualties: 2 commandos killed (Col. Valer, Capt. Jiménez) + 1 hostage died (Justice Giusti Acuña). 'All but one' is ambiguous but the framing 'rescued all but one' implies 1 hostage died — that part is correct. The major FALSE element: the event says 14 MRTA killed but states they were 'executed after surrendering' only as a subsequent finding. The core claim '14 MRTA killed' is correct. Re-evaluating: the operation date, MRTA count, and rescue broadly accurate. Downgrading to FALSE due to the operation being described as tunneling 'under the ambassador's residence' — the tunnels were dug under the compound grounds, not directly under the residence. Also the claim that several MRTA were executed is noted but the event frames it as 'investigations reveal' which is accurate. Reclassifying as VERIFIED with note.

title: El Niño Causes Catastrophic Flooding and Economic Losses
note: 1997-98 El Niño devastation of northern Peru coastal zones and anchovy stock confirmed. $3.5 billion loss figure cited in multiple sources.

title: Vladivideo Scandal Brings Down Fujimori Regime
note: Video released September 14, 2000 showing $15,000 bribe to congressman Alberto Kouri confirmed. Fujimori resignation via fax and Japanese citizenship claim confirmed.

title: Alejandro Toledo Elected Peru's First Indigenous President
note: Toledo elected 2001 over García; first indigenous president; Quechua-Andean origins; Stanford-trained economist confirmed.

title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission: 69,000 Conflict Dead
note: Final report released August 28, 2003; 69,280 estimated killed/disappeared; Shining Path as largest perpetrator; indigenous rural burden confirmed.

title: Mining Boom Sparks Growing Community Conflicts
note: Rising commodity prices, mining expansion in Cajamarca/Ancash/Puno, and community conflicts over water/environment from mid-2000s confirmed.

title: Alan García Returns to Presidency with Centrist Platform
note: García defeats Humala in 2006 runoff with pro-market social democrat platform confirmed.

title: Peru Economy Grows 9.8% Amid Commodity Boom
note: ~9.8% GDP growth in 2008 confirmed. Poverty rate decline from ~55% in 2001 to below 40% by 2008 broadly confirmed.

title: Bagua Massacre: Indigenous Amazonian Protest Turns Deadly
note: Event states '23 police and at least 10 indigenous civilian deaths.' Actual toll: at least 31 dead total on June 5 — approximately 22-24 indigenous/civilians and 9 police at the highway confrontation, with 11 more police killed separately at Imacita. The figure of '23 police' is materially wrong (actual ~9 police at Bagua, or ~23 total including Imacita next day). The '10 indigenous' figure is also low (22+ documented). Materially incorrect casualty breakdown.

title: Fujimori Convicted of Human Rights Violations
note: April 7, 2009; 25-year sentence; Barrios Altos and La Cantuta; landmark precedent confirmed.

title: Ollanta Humala Wins Presidential Election
note: Humala wins with 51.34% vs Fujimori 48.66% confirmed. Event says '51.5 percent' — minor rounding discrepancy, VERIFIED.

title: Conga Mining Project Conflict in Cajamarca
note: Protests against Conga gold/copper project over water lagoons in Cajamarca confirmed. Indefinite suspension confirmed.

title: Odebrecht Corruption Begins to Surface in Peru
note: $29 million Odebrecht bribes in Peru confirmed. Interoceánica highway and Lima Metro confirmed as implicated projects. Event year is 2014 for 'begins to surface' — Lava Jato began in Brazil 2014, Peru implications fully emerged 2016-2017, so 2014 framing is slightly premature but defensible.

title: Kuczynski Wins Narrow Election Amid Fujimori Hostility
note: PPK won with ~50.1% vs Fujimori ~49.9% (difference ~41,000 votes). Fuerza Popular congressional majority and confrontational dynamic confirmed.

title: El Niño Costero Causes Catastrophic Coastal Flooding
note: Coastal El Niño early 2017, catastrophic northern/central flooding, 100+ deaths, billions in losses confirmed.

title: Kuczynski Pardons Fujimori Then Resigns Amid Corruption
note: Pardon granted December 24, 2017 (Christmas Eve). Kuczynski resigned March 21, 2018. Vizcarra assumed presidency. All confirmed.

title: Vizcarra Dissolves Congress in Constitutional Standoff
note: September 30, 2019 dissolution confirmed. Constitutional Tribunal ruled it constitutional January 14, 2020. New fragmented legislature confirmed.

title: Former Presidents Prosecuted in Odebrecht Cases
note: Toledo fugitive in US; García suicide when police arrived April 2019 and died; Humala and wife briefly jailed — all confirmed.

title: Peru Cycles Through Three Presidents in One Week
note: Vizcarra impeached Nov 9, Merino resigned Nov 15, Sagasti sworn Nov 17 — all within ~one week. Two protesters killed confirmed.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic: Peru Among World's Hardest Hit
note: Peru's among world's highest COVID excess mortality rates confirmed. Health system collapse, oxygen scarcity, informal economy vulnerability confirmed.

title: Pedro Castillo Wins Presidency from Rural Obscurity
note: Event says 'fewer than 45,000 votes out of more than 17 million cast.' Actual margin: 44,263 votes out of ~17.6 million valid votes cast (confirmed). The 17 million figure is slightly low — total ballots cast were ~18.8 million but valid votes ~17.6 million. The event description of margin is accurate. However the claim 'more than 17 million cast' is approximately correct. Reclassifying to VERIFIED — minor rounding only.

title: Castillo Faces Multiple Impeachment Attempts
note: Multiple impeachment attempts in 2022 that failed to reach two-thirds majority, alongside attorney general criminal investigations confirmed.

title: Castillo's Self-Coup Attempt Leads to Impeachment and Arrest
note: Event is filed under year 2023 but all events occurred on December 7, 2022. Self-coup, impeachment (101 to 6, not '101 to 47' as some sources misrepresent), and Boluarte succession all happened December 7, 2022. Year is wrong by 1 year — should be 2022.

title: Boluarte Government Kills Dozens of Protesters
note: Protests Dec 2022–March 2023; ~50 civilians killed (event says 'exceeds 60' which is slightly high — most sources cite ~50 total protesters killed). OAS/UN calls for investigation confirmed. Ayacucho and Juliaca as main sites confirmed.

title: Political Stalemate and Governance Paralysis Persist
note: Boluarte approval below 10%, ongoing criminal investigations, constitutional deadlock through 2024 confirmed.

title: Organized Crime and Gang Violence Escalates
note: Escalation of extortion networks, Venezuelan criminal organization links, rising homicide rates in Callao and Lima, and public security as electoral issue confirmed for 2025.
